guidance_summary:
GUIDANCE ANALYSIS: Hays plc — H1 2025

METRIC: Germany Temp & Contracting year-on-year net-fee headwind
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Likely to be modest
UNIT: qualitative year-on-year net-fee headwind
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Q3 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Quarter
BASIS: Germany Temp & Contracting; year-on-year; supported by easier comparatives
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Germany Temp & Contracting average hours worked remained sequentially stable.
- Easier prior-year comparative in Q3 FY25.
- Automotive-related weakness in German Temp remains a headwind, partly offset by greater resilience in Contracting.

METRIC: Group net-fee growth working-day effect
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.1% positive impact on year-on-year net-fee growth
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Q3 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Quarter
BASIS: Group year-on-year net-fee growth; calendar/working-day effect
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Easter falls entirely in Q4 FY25, whereas it was evenly split between Q3 and Q4 in FY24.

METRIC: Group net-fee growth working-day effect
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.1% headwind to year-on-year net-fee growth
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Q4 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Quarter
BASIS: Group year-on-year net-fee growth; calendar/working-day effect
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Easter falls entirely in Q4 FY25, whereas it was evenly split between Q3 and Q4 in FY24.

METRIC: Group consultant headcount
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Remain broadly stable
UNIT: qualitative closing headcount
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Q3 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Quarter
BASIS: Group consultant headcount
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Capacity reductions are planned in more difficult markets.
- Management will make selected investments where opportunities exist.
- Management considers consultant capacity appropriate for current market conditions.

METRIC: Total Group headcount
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Decrease slightly
UNIT: qualitative headcount
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Q3 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Quarter
BASIS: Total Group headcount
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Continuation of back-office efficiency programmes.

METRIC: Cost base per period
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Further reduce
UNIT: qualitative cost base per period
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: H2 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Half Year
BASIS: Structural cost efficiencies; reductions expected largely in non-consultant areas
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Further back-office efficiency programmes and operational restructuring are in progress.
- Consultant headcount is expected to remain broadly stable, so expected H2 reductions are largely from non-consultant areas.

METRIC: Further exceptional costs
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Expected to incur further exceptional costs
UNIT: qualitative exceptional costs
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: H2 FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Half Year
BASIS: Exceptional restructuring and transformation costs
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Ongoing multi-year restructuring programme.
- Technology Transformation and Finance Transformation programmes.
- Further operational and back-office actions planned in H2.

METRIC: Net finance charge
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.£13 million
UNIT: £ million
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Net finance charge
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Higher average drawings on the revolving credit facility increased net bank interest payable.

METRIC: Effective tax rate
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.32%, assuming no material change in geographic mix of profits
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Group pre-exceptional effective tax rate
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Forecast assumes no material change in the geographic mix of profits.

METRIC: Capital expenditure
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.£25 million
UNIT: £ million
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Full-year capital expenditure
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Continued investment in infrastructure and cyber security.

METRIC: Enterprise net fees
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Approximately £225 million to £250 million
UNIT: £ million
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: FY25
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Enterprise net fees
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Growth within existing clients through higher fill rates, headcount investment and geographic expansion.
- New client wins, including first-generation MSP outsourcing opportunities and wins from competitors.
- Retention of key contracts supported by service quality.
- Management stated Enterprise has a substantial bid pipeline.

METRIC: Structural back-office efficiency cost savings
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.£30 million per annum structural back-office efficiency cost savings
UNIT: £ million per annum
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: By the end of FY27
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Multi Year
BASIS: Structural back-office savings, notably finance and technology functions
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Finance transformation in the Americas.
- Global technology outsourcing/transformation project.
- Restructuring of the global marketing function.
- Further standardisation, globalisation and shared-service-centre expansion.

METRIC: Pension scheme expenses and true-up costs
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.£6 million
UNIT: £ million
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Next 12–18 months through to final scheme buy-out
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Date Range
BASIS: Expenses and true-up costs following the defined-benefit pension scheme full buy-in
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Administration expenses and potential post-buy-in true-up costs are expected before final scheme buy-out.

METRIC: Final pension scheme buy-out and wind-up
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Positioned to transition to final buy-out and wind-up, subject to Trustee approval
UNIT: qualitative milestone
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: FY26
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Defined-benefit pension scheme
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The December 2024 full buy-in insured the remaining scheme obligations.
- Financial and demographic risks relating to scheme liabilities are now 100% insured.
- Transition remains subject to Trustee approval.

METRIC: Pension buy-in cash-flow benefit
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: c.£19 million per annum
UNIT: £ million per annum
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: From FY26
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Multi Year
BASIS: Free-cash-flow benefit from cessation of pension-deficit contributions
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- No further pension-deficit contributions are required following the December 2024 full buy-in.

METRIC: Business-line conversion rate
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: At least 25%
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Normal market conditions
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Other
BASIS: Pre-central-cost conversion rate; net fees converted into pre-exceptional operating profit
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects operational rigour, business-line prioritisation and resource allocation to support normalised profitability.

METRIC: Group conversion rate
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 22–25%
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Normal market conditions
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Other
BASIS: Group conversion rate; net fees converted into pre-exceptional operating profit
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Target reflects expected benefit from structural cost savings, improved operating efficiency and normal market conditions.

METRIC: UK&I reassigned-consultant fee productivity
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: More than £10k fee productivity per period
UNIT: £k per period
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Within 12 months
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Date Range
BASIS: More than 50 Healthcare and Social Care consultants transferred to Construction & Property and Senior Finance
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Consultants were reallocated from lower-productivity roles to specialisms with higher expected productivity.

METRIC: UK&I reassigned-consultant conversion rate
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Mid-teens percentage conversion rate
UNIT: %
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Within 12 months
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Date Range
BASIS: More than 50 Healthcare and Social Care consultants transferred to Construction & Property and Senior Finance
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Reallocation targets specialisms with stronger productivity and conversion potential.

METRIC: Long-term operating profit objective
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Return to, and then exceed, previous peak profits of £250 million
UNIT: £ million operating profit
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Long-term objective
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Multi Year
BASIS: Group operating profit objective
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Business-line prioritisation and optimised consultant resource allocation.
- Scaling the eight Focus countries.
- Structural cost savings and a more scalable back-office function.
- Expected cyclical recovery and higher drop-through of fee growth to profit.

METRIC: Growth relationship under the Golden Rule
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: Operating profit growth should be greater than net-fee growth, which should in turn exceed headcount growth
UNIT: qualitative growth hierarchy
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Through the cycle
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Multi Year
BASIS: Group operating model and investment discipline
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management intends to retain structural cost savings.
- Disciplined consultant-headcount investment.
- Focus on higher-skilled roles, operational efficiency and profit growth.

METRIC: Target net cash position
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: £100 million
UNIT: £ million
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Not explicitly stated
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Not Stated
BASIS: Capital-allocation framework target net cash position
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management's free-cash-flow priorities include maintaining a strong balance sheet.

METRIC: Core dividend cover target
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 2–3x EPS
UNIT: times pre-exceptional EPS
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Not explicitly stated
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Not Stated
BASIS: Core dividend policy
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management describes the core dividend as intended to be sustainable, progressive and appropriate.

events.title: Hays Q3 FY25 trading update reports continued net-fee contraction
events.summary: Hays reported that Q3 FY25 group net fees declined 9% year on year on a like-for-like basis. Temp & Contracting fees fell 6% and Permanent fees fell 14%. German temporary staffing remained subdued because of automotive exposure, while permanent hiring was weak amid longer hiring cycles. Hays reduced consultant headcount and progressed structural back-office efficiencies, lowering its periodic cost base to about £76 million, while retaining FY25 operating-profit guidance in line with consensus at that time.
source_headlines: Hays reports Q3 FY25 net-fee decline as permanent hiring and German automotive-linked temp demand remain weak

events.title: UK recruitment survey reports April contraction in placements, temporary billings and vacancies
events.summary: The KPMG/REC UK Report on Jobs reported that permanent placements and temporary billings both declined in April 2025, while demand for workers and vacancies fell further. Recruiters cited weak employer confidence and tighter hiring budgets. Temporary-pay growth accelerated to an 11-month high, with respondents pointing to recent minimum-wage increases.
source_headlines: KPMG/REC survey reports continued UK recruitment contraction and falling vacancies in April

events.title: Hays cuts FY25 operating-profit expectation following Q4 deterioration in permanent recruitment
events.summary: Hays said fourth-quarter activity had weakened sequentially, led by low client and candidate confidence and broad global weakness in permanent recruitment. It expected Q4 like-for-like net fees to decline 9%, including a 14% decline in permanent fees, and reduced expected FY25 pre-exceptional operating profit to about £45 million from then company-compiled consensus of £56.4 million. Germany was expected to decline 5%, with a subdued automotive sector weighing on temporary and permanent hiring; UK&I and ANZ permanent markets had also weakened.
source_headlines: Hays cuts FY25 profit expectation to about £45m after a broad-based deterioration in permanent recruitment

events.title: Hays FY25 results confirm lower net fees and profit and record restructuring and transformation charges
events.summary: For FY25, Hays reported net fees of £972.4 million, down 13% reported and 11% like for like, and pre-exceptional operating profit of £45.6 million, down 57% reported. It recorded £30.7 million of exceptional charges: £17.7 million for restructuring and £13.0 million for technology and finance transformation. The company completed office and business-line closures, refinanced its revolving credit facility, reduced the total dividend to 1.24p per share, and targeted a further roughly £45 million of annual structural cost savings by FY29. It said the pension buy-in would be materially positive for free cash flow from FY26.
source_headlines: Hays FY25 results confirm steep profit decline, restructuring charges and a revised capital-allocation framework

events.title: Hays Q1 FY26 net fees decline as staffing reductions and cost actions continue
events.summary: Hays reported that Q1 FY26 group net fees fell 8% year on year on a like-for-like basis. Temp & Contracting fees declined 5% and permanent-recruitment fees fell 13%, with permanent markets still affected by longer hiring cycles. Consultant net-fee productivity increased 7%, consultant headcount fell 15% year on year, and the periodic cost base improved to about £74 million. Net debt was about £40 million at quarter-end, reflecting normal seasonal outflows and payment timing.
source_headlines: Hays Q1 FY26 net fees fall 8%; staffing reductions and cost actions partly offset weak permanent hiring

events.title: Germany approves statutory minimum-wage increase effective January 2026
events.summary: Germany's cabinet approved an increase in the statutory minimum wage to €13.90 per hour from 1 January 2026, up from €12.82. The ministry described the first-stage increase as 8.42%.
source_headlines: German government approves increase in statutory minimum wage to €13.90 per hour from January 2026

events.title: Hays reports Q2 FY26 fee decline and expects about £20 million of first-half operating profit
events.summary: Reuters reported that Hays' Q2 FY26 like-for-like net fees fell 10%, versus analysts' expectation of a 9% decline. Hays expected pre-exceptional operating profit for the six months ended December 2025 of about £20 million, down about 21.6% year on year. Reuters attributed the quarterly weakness principally to technology and engineering hiring in Germany, amid persistently weak global hiring and delayed recruitment decisions.
source_headlines: Hays posts a larger-than-expected Q2 FY26 fee decline as German technology and engineering hiring weakens

events.title: German Federal Employment Agency reports 2025 vacancies at a 25-year low
events.summary: Germany's Federal Employment Agency said labor demand continued to decline during 2025 amid weak economic development. Average registered vacancies were 632,000, down 62,000 from 2024, while total reported jobs fell to 1.461 million, the lowest level in 25 years. The agency also reported higher unemployment and elevated use of short-time work.
source_headlines: German Federal Employment Agency says 2025 job vacancies fell to their lowest level in 25 years

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Basis alignment: previous reported actual is H1 FY25 (six months ended 31 December 2024) net fees of £496.0m; target is standalone H1 FY26 (six months ended 31 December 2025). The 14 January 2026 update gave direct H1-period evidence rather than FY guidance: management described c.£45m year-on-year fee decline in H1, consistent with Q1 LFL net fees -8% and Q2 LFL net fees -10%. Therefore no mechanical FY-to-H1 pro-rating is used. Forecast H1 FY26 net fees = £496.0m - £45.0m = £451.0m. Total projected change = £451.0m - £496.0m = -£45.0m.

assumptions: The c.£45m H1 net-fee decline stated on the 14 January call is treated as the central direct H1 guide.

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Basis alignment: previous reported actual is H1 FY25 pre-exceptional basic EPS of 0.81p; target is H1 FY26 pre-exceptional basic EPS. Management guided only H1 pre-exceptional operating profit, so EPS is bottom-up derived. Forecast pre-exceptional PBT = £20.0m operating profit - £6.5m net finance charge = £13.5m. Using H1 FY25's disclosed 32.1% pre-exceptional tax rate and unchanged 1,588.5m weighted-average basic shares: EPS = [£13.5m x (1 - 0.321) / 1,588.5m] x 100 = 0.577p, rounded to 0.58p. Total projected change = 0.58p - 0.81p = -0.23p.

event_contributions.affected_line: Operating profit, interest/net finance charge, tax and weighted-average shares
event_contributions.transmission_path: Lower net fees partly offset by structural cost savings -> H1 pre-exceptional operating profit of c.£20m -> less assumed finance charge -> pre-exceptional PBT -> tax -> earnings attributable to ordinary shareholders -> basic EPS.
assumptions: Direct H1 pre-exceptional operating-profit guidance is £20.0m.
Net finance charge is held at the H1 FY25 actual £6.5m because no new H1 FY26 finance-charge guidance was supplied; year-end net cash reduces downside risk but does not support precision.
Pre-exceptional tax rate is held at H1 FY25 actual 32.1%.
Weighted-average basic shares are held at H1 FY25 actual 1,588.5m; the employee-share treasury programme is not assumed material enough to change displayed EPS.
event_contributions.calculation: DIRECT H1 ROUTE for EBIT, then bottom-up EPS: PBT = £20.0m - £6.5m = £13.5m. Pre-exceptional PAT = £13.5m x 67.9% = £9.1665m. EPS = (£9.1665m / 1,588.5m) x 100 = 0.577p, rounded 0.58p. Contribution versus 0.81p actual = -0.233p, rounded -0.23p.

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Basis alignment: previous reported actual is H1 FY25 pre-exceptional operating profit of £25.5m; target is H1 FY26 pre-exceptional operating profit for the six months ended 31 December 2025. Management provided direct standalone H1 guidance of c.£20.0m, so FY phasing is not required. Forecast = £20.0m. Total projected change = £20.0m - £25.5m = -£5.5m.

event_contributions.transmission_path: c.£45m lower H1 net fees -> lower gross contribution; consultant productivity gains, headcount reductions and cost savings -> lower operating expense -> pre-exceptional operating profit of c.£20m.
